newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army says over 500 rebels killed,wounded.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army says over 500 rebels killed,wounded.

text.p: Sri Lankan forces have killed or wounded more than 500 Tamil Tiger guerrillas in a fresh offensive on the rebels' northern stronghold, military officials said on Wednesday.

"The aim of this operation is to draw and kill as many terrorists as possible," military spokesman Brigadier Sarath Munasinghe said, referring to the four-day-old offensive against the separatist Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
"According to estimates made by ground troops, over 75 terrorists were killed on Tuesday and more than 100 wounded," he told a news conference.

The Defence Ministry said more than 330 rebels were either killed or wounded on Sunday and Monday in fighting near the town of Kilinochchi, the northern entry point to the Tigers' jungle territory of the Wanni.
The army lost 58 soldiers and had 115 wounded near Kilinochchi since Sunday when they launched the offensive after more than a month's lull in the conflict.

The LTTE, seeking an independent homeland for minority Tamils, on Wednesday killed 15 more soldiers in an attack in the army-controlled northern Jaffna Peninsula, north of Kilinochchi, a ministry statement said.
"In Jaffna, terrorists activated a claymore mine against a vehicle carrying security forces personnel. Fifteen soldiers were killed and four more wounded in the explosion," it said.
Defence analysts said the rebels could launch more attacks in army-controlled areas to divert attention from fighting near their stronghold.
Military officials earlier said security forces had renewed air and artillery strikes near Kilinochchi, 285 km (180 miles) north of Colombo, in a bid to break through guerrilla resistance.
Munasinghe said two columns of troops were advancing from the road junction town of Paranthan, six km (four miles) north of Kilinochchi, in a pincer-shape offensive.
One column of troops was now five km (three miles) southeast of Paranthan while on the other flank, troops had advanced seven km (four miles) southwest of the town, he said.
Several army divisions were taking part in the assault, and the rebels were resisting mainly with mortars, he said.
Analysts said government troops were trying a pincer move to outflank the rebels, who were well dug in at Kilinochchi.

The Voice of Tigers radio, mouthpiece of the LTTE, reported heavy fighting in the Kilinochchi base and said many civilians had been killed, but a military officer said the strikes were focused on identified enemy positions.
Diplomats said the army casualties indicated that the LTTE were putting up strong resistance.

Military officials said they had stepped up surveillance in the Jaffna lagoon between the Jaffna peninsula and the mainland, just north of Kilinochchi, to deter rebel attempts to land reinforcements by boat.
"Kilinochchi is important for them. It is the last major town in their hands with a hospital and other infrastructure," one officer said.
The army has said it wants to reopen the highway connecting Jaffna and Colombo, which passes through a large swathe of rebel-held territory separating Jaffna and the mainland.
The military has been targeting Kilinochchi since the LTTE overran the northeastern Mullaitivu camp in July, killing or capturing almost its entire garrison of 1,400 men.
It was the military's worst setback in the 13-year war, in which the government says more than 50,000 people have died.
